bull.b: Consistent, sizable free cash flow (~$1.17B TTM) and positive operating cash (~$1.24B TTM) provide durable funding for R&D, buybacks and strategic investments. Strong cash conversion cushions the business through GAAP losses and reduces reliance on external capital over the medium term.

Accelerating product revenue (+34% YoY) combined with high net revenue retention (126%) and expansion of $1M+/ $10M+ customers indicates durable upsell and stickiness. This structural demand profile supports predictable consumption growth and long-term revenue compounding.

Large multi-year deals (notably a $6B AWS expansion and a $200M OpenAI pact) deepen cloud-provider alignment and channel reach, lowering unit costs and increasing customer lock-in. These partnerships structurally improve cost levers and accelerate enterprise AI adoption on the platform.

bear.b: Leverage has risen materially (debt-to-equity ~1.35–1.42), increasing financial rigidity while GAAP losses persist. Elevated debt raises refinancing and interest-cost risk, and constrains strategic optionality if free cash flow weakens or growth slows over the next several quarters.

Despite strong gross margins, Snowflake remains meaningfully unprofitable on a GAAP basis (TTM net margin ~-24%) with deeply negative ROE. Persistent operating expense intensity means profitability depends on sustained revenue scale and disciplined cost control over multiple quarters.

Native AI adoption boosts usage but carries lower gross margins and creates cost pressure. Customers may throttle consumption to control bills, and increasing booking concentration in Q4 amplifies timing and renewal risk. These factors can compress margins and reduce near-term visibility.
